chapter: Chicago's South Side night life in the early 1920s
title: Map of the South Side cabarets: Dreamland, Sunset, Columbia Tavern
summary: Caldwell lists the cabarets and after-hours places along State Street from 31st to 35th, and who led the bands.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, where were they? All on State Street?
No, they were all up -- these big clubs were mostly outside of Dreamland. Dreamland was on State Street between 35th and 36th.

That's where Freddy Keppard played. He had a group there, and big band there, Freddy Keppard and Nate Brady. Auto Café was on one side of the street, and the Taylor Cafe was on the other side. That's where Sammy Stewart brought his band from Columbus, Ohio. And up about two blocks near Kermit Avenue was the Sunset. That was Carl Carroll Dickerson. Then they had the (unintelligible) the Radio Inn.
Now, the Radio Inn is a new one on me. Who did you say played there?

Well, Buster Bailey -- like we'd finish our job like early in the night, and this was an after hour place. See, and they'd go right -- it broadcasted all the time (unintelligible) Tatum, Buster and them used to pick up the telephone and listen to the band and all like that, and like the Fiume Cafe --
Fiume? How do you spell that?

Right. That was after hours. And like going down to 31st Street, they had the Schiller's Inn, which was another nice offside cabaret; where we worked was at Columbia Tavern off 35th -- on 31st and State underneath the

Columbia Hotel. Then you had a place down further -- Jack Johnson used to own (unintelligible) to them. Well, there was a cabaret and after hours joint. Now, that's down in that part of the section. Then on -- over going toward the lake there was the Royal Aurora Garden. That's where Joe Oliver Harvey had his band. And that was -- in that particular section -- then up State Street, going back to 35th Street, all the big places was there, like Entertainers, the Auto Cafe, Dreamland, Sunset, Entertainers (unintelligible).
